title: Getting around
goal: Ask for and follow directions, take buses and autorickshaws, and tell a driver where to go and stop.
intro:
In Kerala you'll get around by bus (private and KSRTC government buses), by **ഓട്ടോ** (autorickshaw), by train, and in the backwaters by boat. Places are usually described by the nearest **ജംഗ്ഷൻ** (junction), temple, church or landmark rather than by street names.

Grammar: **imperatives** — informal, polite and very polite — and the endings for **direction**: 'to', 'towards', 'from', 'as far as'.

vocab.note: 'To the left': ഇടത്തോട്ട്. Also ഇടതുവശത്ത് 'on the left side'.
Bus stand: ബസ് സ്റ്റാൻഡ്; bus stop: ബസ് സ്റ്റോപ്പ്.

vocab.en: to get on, board; to climb; to enter
to get off; to go down

phrases.en: How far is it from here?
Which bus goes to Fort Kochi?
Will you go as far as the junction? (to an auto driver)
Could you put the meter on?

grammar.title: Imperatives: informal, polite and very polite
grammar.body:
• **Informal** (to friends, children; നീ-level): the bare stem — drop -ുക; if the stem ends in a consonant, add the half-u: പോകുക → **പോ**, വരുക → **വാ** (irregular), നോക്കുക → **നോക്ക്**, ഇരിക്കുക → **ഇരിക്ക്**, നിർത്തുക → **നിർത്ത്**.
• **Polite** (നിങ്ങൾ-level): **-ഊ**: **പോകൂ**, **വരൂ**, **നോക്കൂ**, **ഇരിക്കൂ**, **നിർത്തൂ**.
• **Softer request**: question form **-ആമോ?** 'could you?': **നിർത്താമോ?** 'could you stop?'. Adding **ഒന്ന്** ('once') softens anything: ഒന്ന് നിർത്താമോ?
• Colloquial pleading: **-അണേ**: ഇവിടെ നിർത്തണേ 'please do stop here'.

Negative: **-അരുത്** 'don't!' (firm) or **-ഏണ്ട** 'no need to' (gentle): പോകരുത് 'don't go!', പോകേണ്ട 'you needn't go'.

grammar.title: Direction: to, towards, from, up to
grammar.body:
• **to (a place)**: **-ഇലേക്ക്** (-ilēkkŭ) for places, or simply the **dative -ക്ക്**: കൊച്ചിയിലേക്ക് / കൊച്ചിക്ക് 'to Kochi', വീട്ടിലേക്ക് 'home(wards)'.
• **towards / in the direction**: **-ഓട്ട്** (-ōṭṭŭ): ഇടത്തോട്ട് 'to the left', മുകളിലോട്ട് 'upwards', എങ്ങോട്ട്? 'where to?', ഇങ്ങോട്ട് 'this way, here', അങ്ങോട്ട് 'that way, there'.
• **from**: **-ഇൽ നിന്ന്**: സ്റ്റേഷനിൽ നിന്ന് 'from the station'.
• **as far as, until**: **വരെ** (vare): ജംഗ്ഷൻ വരെ 'up to the junction'; രാത്രി വരെ 'until night'.
• **via**: **വഴി**: കോട്ടയം വഴി 'via Kottayam'.

examples.en: Does this bus go to Thrissur?

examples.native: വിമാനത്താവളത്തിൽ നിന്ന് നഗരത്തിലേക്ക് ഒരു മണിക്കൂർ ആണ്.
examples.roman: vimānattāvaḷattil ninnŭ nagarattilēkkŭ oru maṇikkūr āṇŭ.
examples.en: It's an hour from the airport to the city.
Go straight up to the bridge.

dialogue.title: Taking an auto
dialogue.setting: Emma flags down an autorickshaw outside Ernakulam South station.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.en: Will you go to Marine Drive?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.en: Could you put the meter on?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.en: OK, done. It's not far, ten minutes.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.en: You need to turn right near that bridge.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.en: I know. Then straight on, right?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: അതെ. ദാ, ആ ബാങ്കിന്റെ മുന്നിൽ നിർത്തൂ.
lines.roman: ate. dā, ā bāṅkinde munnil nirttū.
lines.en: Yes. There — stop in front of that bank, please.

culture: Directions are given by landmarks: 'go past the temple, turn left at the junction near the church'. When asking, address the person as ചേട്ടാ / ചേച്ചീ. On private buses the conductor (കണ്ടക്ടർ) collects fares on board; buses can be very fast, so hold on, and women traditionally sit at the front. Ask an auto driver for the meter (മീറ്റർ) or agree the fare before you get in.

tip.title: Telling someone where to go
tip.body:
- Polite 'please do': swap **-ുക** for **-ഊ**: പോകുക → **പോകൂ**, തിരിയുക → **തിരിയൂ**.
- To a friend or child, just the stem: **പോ**, **തിരി**, **നോക്ക്**; 'come' is **വാ**.
- 'Don't!' is **-അരുത്** (പോകരുത്); 'no need to' is **-ഏണ്ട** (പോകേണ്ട).
- Directions: **ഇടത്തോട്ട്** 'to the left', **വലത്തോട്ട്** 'to the right', **നേരെ** 'straight on'.

sentences.en: Go straight on, please.
Turn right there, please.
Turn left at the next road. (informal)
Come this way. (informal)
Excuse me, is this the right way?
Don't play on the road!
There's a small road on the left.
My house is on the right side of the road.
Should I turn right or left?
No need to go that way, this one's quicker.
Go slowly, the road's bad here.
Look straight ahead, don't look at your phone!

tip.title: To, from and as far as
tip.body:
- **to** a place: **-ഇലേക്ക്** (ബാങ്കിലേക്ക്), or the short **-ക്ക്** (കൊച്ചിക്ക്).
- **from**: **-ഇൽ നിന്ന്**: ജംഗ്ഷനിൽ നിന്ന് 'from the junction', ഇവിടെ നിന്ന് 'from here'.
- **as far as / until**: **വരെ** after the word: പാലം **വരെ**, ആറ് മണി **വരെ**.
- **-ം** words take **-ത്ത്-** first: അമ്പലം → അമ്പല**ത്തിലേക്ക്**.

sentences.en: I'm going to the bank.

sentences.native: പാലം വരെ നടക്കൂ, പിന്നെ ഇടത്തോട്ട് തിരിയൂ.
sentences.roman: pālam vare naṭakkū, pinne iṭattōṭṭŭ tiriyū.
sentences.en: Walk as far as the bridge, then turn left.
The bank isn't far from the junction.
Which way is it to the temple?

sentences.native: ഞായറാഴ്ച ഞങ്ങൾ പള്ളിയിൽ നിന്ന് നേരെ വീട്ടിലേക്ക് വരും.
sentences.roman: ñāyaṟāḻcha ñaṅṅaḷ paḷḷiyil ninnŭ nēre vīṭṭilēkkŭ varum.
sentences.en: On Sundays we come straight home from church.

sentences.native: ഇവിടെ നിന്ന് അമ്പലം വരെ നടന്നു പോകാം.
sentences.roman: iviṭe ninnŭ ambalam vare naṭannu pōkām.
sentences.en: We can walk from here to the temple.
Where's the shop? It's next to the bridge.
Is it far? No, just five minutes.

sentences.native: ഞാൻ ആറ് മണി വരെ ബാങ്കിൽ ആണ്.
sentences.roman: ñān āṟŭ maṇi vare bāṅkil āṇŭ.
sentences.en: I'm at the bank until six.
You have to turn right at the junction.

sentences.native: കടയിൽ നിന്ന് ഒരു കിലോ അരി വേണം.
sentences.roman: kaṭayil ninnŭ oru kilō ari vēṇam.
sentences.en: I need a kilo of rice from the shop.

tip.title: Will it…? -ഉം and -ഉമോ
tip.body:
- Timetable talk uses the **-ഉം** form, 'will / does': ബസ് എത്ര മണിക്ക് **എത്തും**?
- Add **-ഓ** for a yes/no question: **പോകുമോ?** 'does it go?', **വൈകുമോ?** 'will it be late?'
- **ഏത്** 'which' goes before the noun: **ഏത് ബസ്**? 'which bus?'
- A ticket 'to' a place uses the short **-ക്ക്**: കൊച്ചി**ക്ക്** ഒരു ടിക്കറ്റ്.

sentences.en: When does the train get in?
Does this bus go to the station?
The bus will be here in ten minutes.
Will the train be late?
The train's here! Come quick!
Two tickets to Kochi.
How much is the ticket?
When will we get to Alappuzha?
Which bus goes to the junction?
I'll go by train tomorrow.
Is the station far from here?

tip.title: Talking to the driver
tip.body:
- Call the driver **ചേട്ടാ** ('big brother!'), the friendly way to address any man a bit older than you.
- Ask with **-ആമോ?** 'could you?': **നിർത്താമോ?**, **പോകാമോ?**; add **ഒന്ന്** to sound softer.
- **-ആം** is 'I'll… / let's…': ഞാൻ ഇവിടെ **ഇറങ്ങാം**, **പോകാം**.
- Get in = **കയറുക**, get out = **ഇറങ്ങുക**.

sentences.en: Could you stop in front of the bank, please?
Could you take me to the station?
Get in, let's go.
We'll get off near the temple.
Could you go a bit faster? I'm late.
Where do you want to get off?

sentences.native: ഇവിടെ അല്ല, ആ കടയുടെ മുന്നിൽ നിർത്തൂ.
sentences.roman: iviṭe alla, ā kaṭayuṭe munnil nirttū.
sentences.en: Not here, stop in front of that shop, please.
Excuse me, you haven't put the meter on.
Let's take an auto, it's too far to walk.
How much is that?
What's this place called?
My hometown is a small village.
Kochi is a big city.
The airport is a long way from the city.
Is there a bus to the airport?
Let's go by boat in Alappuzha.
What time is the boat?
There's no bank in the village, you have to go into town.
There's no room to stop an auto here.
